messages.subject: ggplot2 web application
parts:
We used ggplot2 in a web application to plot live stock data from
Yahoo Finance. It nicely demonstrates the power of R and ggplot in the
context of an internet application. The web application is publicly
available, and you can find at my homepage: www.jeroenooms.com. Give
it a try (but not all at the same time please :) and let us know what
you think!

messages.author: ba9318fcb03a20d0
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 web application
parts:
Hi Jeroen,
The graphs are nice, the interface is very slow. At least when I tried
it.
I gave a talk at DSC in Copenhagen, addressing some of these issues. For
instance
if I split the workspace into two graphs, and try and plot another
company in the second
window, it does not load, is that a bug? Hmmm, now that I reloaded the
application
it works. I am wondering if you can solve some of these problems using
some caching?
If you have an application at one end streaming the data and the user
only interfaces
with your data base, then you don't have to worry about web delays
getting the data.
Anyway just a thought. As I am sure you are aware, the biggest issue is
passing data,
and the stochastic nature of web connections. Are you using google tools
for the interface?
Oh, and it would be nice if you had controls to control the degrees of
freedom in the smoother,
For some of the "real" jumps it is too smooth.

but nice.

Nicholas

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 web application
parts:
Nicholas,

thanks for your feedback. I am using rapache to connect the httpd to
R. However, the server seems to have an issue when multiple R requests
are done in a short period. That than results in an error in de httpd,
and your figure not loading correctly. After a refresh it often does
return a correct plot, with a bit of luck. I am looking into this.

I am using ExtJS for the interface. The smoothing is done by the
ggplot2 package, I am not sure there is an option to adjust the
smoothing parameter, but I'll keep it in mind.

Thanks again :)

Jeroen
